intro.title: Build typed analytics event catalog
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed analytics event catalog to safely track user interactions in an application. You will learn to use TypeScript's core feature—type safety—to define a set of possible events, ensuring that only valid event names and data are logged. This involves creating custom types, interfaces, and a function to record events, which helps prevent runtime errors. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe system for managing analytics events in your projects.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building robust analytics systems in applications like e-commerce dashboards, where tracking user interactions (e.g., button clicks, form submissions, page views) must be type-safe and consistent. Developers use typed event catalogs to ensure events like 'add_to_cart' or 'checkout_start' are properly defined with required properties, preventing runtime errors in tools like Google Analytics or Mixpanel. In practice, this enables teams to maintain a single source of truth for analytics events across features such as user onboarding flows, A/B testing panels, or admin modals, improving data reliability and developer collaboration.
